paragraphs: Rabbi Acha son of Rav Chiyya: [Nedarim 10b](https://www.sefaria.org/Nedarim.10b.9).
Rabbi Ami bar Chiyya: [Zevachim 105b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.105b.10-12), and [Avodah Zarah 51b](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.51b.15).
Rabbi Binyamin bar Chiyya: end of Rosh Hashanah.
Rav Yosef bar Chiyya (Rav Yosef without further designation): [Chullin 18b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.18b.4).
Rabbi Yitzchak bar Chiyya Ketubah: [Yerushalmi Pesachim 1:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Pesachim.1.8.9), followed by the supplied י.
Rabbi Levi bar Chiyya: end of Berakhot.

Rav Mesharshiya son of Rav Chiyya: Chullin 47. Mar Ukva bar Chiyya: [Yevamot 63b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.63b.7). Mar bar Chiyya: [Bava Batra 165b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.165b.10). Anan bar Chiyya: [Yevamot 116a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.116a.3).
Rav Shmuel bar Chiyya: [Bava Metzia 72b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.72b.16). Shimon bar Chiyya: [Yerushalmi Eruvin 5:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Eruvin.5.5.3).
Rabbi Tanchum bar Chiyya: Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan, chapter 3, halakhah 7.[^3]

notes.text: The chapter/halakhah locations are Jerusalem Talmud. כתובה is kept as the accompanying epithet Ketubah; the final י after halakhah8 remains literal rather than proof of a specific pagination system. Unsided Shabbat47/Chullin47 are not assigned a new side.

This is a collective patronymic index. The directly consulted Nedarim 10b names Rav Acha son of Rav Chiyya addressing Rav Ashi; it does not establish one father for every person in the list. Ketubah and the supplied final י are retained without a new pagination claim.

The consulted Avodah Zarah gives Rav Assi bar Chiyya, beside Ami in Zevachim and Hyman’s cross-reference. In Yerushalmi Pesachim the text gives Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rabbi Chiyya Ketubah. The individual notices leave the collective list intact.

The linked conversion story names Oshaya son of Rabbi Chiyya in Rav Safra’s version. Rav Yosef’s version instead says Oshaya bar Rabbi. The alternatives belong to this one notice in Hyman’s patronymic list.
